alumni.name: Stan Green
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Football Captain. Boston Herald and Boston Post All Scholastic team his senior season. Went on to play college football at Columbia.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: John "Iron Mike" Harrington
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Two-time football captain. Boston Herald, Boston Globe, WESX, and North Shore All Scholastic team his senior season. Also an excellent baseball player. Athletic career ended after his senior season due to an accident. One of the greatest athletes to come out of Saugus.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Art Statuto
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1989.

Helped lead the Sachems to the 1941 Class C state championship. Went on to play college football at Notre Dame, where he was a member of their 1946 and 1947 National Champion football teams. He was selected to the 1948 college football All-Star Team. After graduating, he played professional football for three seasons with the Buffalo Bills (AAFC) and Los Angeles Rams (NFL) at the center position.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1989

alumni.name: Doug Waybright
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Won State Championship in 1941 during his sophomore season. Was Captain his senior season. A 1943 Essex County All-Star. Went on to play college football at Notre Dame (1945, 1947-1949). Member of the 1947 and 1949 National Championship teams at Notre Dame. After college he served in the military before he returned to Saugus, where he was very active in youth sports. He was so beloved by the town that when he died at the young age of 38, officials named a new elementary school in his honor.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1988

alumni.name: Art Spinney
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Went on to play college football at Boston College where he was Captain his senior season (1949). A 1972 Inductee into the Boston College Athletic Hall of Fame.
Played in the NFL for the Baltimore Colts (1950, 1953-1960) where he won several accolades:
3x All Pro (1958 - 1960)
2x Pro Bowl (1959 - 1960)
2x NFL Champion (1958 - 1959)
Was the Offensive Line Coach for the Boston Patriots from 1962 - 1968.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: George Laskey
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

2x Sgt. Arthur Defranzo Player of the Year Award winner (1946-1947), Thomas Atkins Memorial Award 1946, named Boston Globe, Boston Post, Lynn Item, and North Shore All Scholastic teams in 1947.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Dan Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1994.

Named a Boston Globe and Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1949.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1994

alumni.name: Salvatore 'Sardi' Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A three-year starter at running back, Sal “Sardi” Nicolo became one of Massachusetts’ most celebrated high school football players. In a memorable senior season, he led his division in touchdowns and points, earned numerous All-Scholastic selections and received honorable mention High School All-American recognition.

His signature Sachems moment came in the 1949 Exchange Bowl, when he caught a 50-yard, over-the-shoulder touchdown pass from his brother Richie to tie Weymouth as time expired. Jimmy Kane’s extra point secured Saugus’ 7–6 victory and the Exchange Bowl championship. Nicolo also excelled in baseball.

He went on to play football at Louisiana State University from 1952 through 1954. His 94-yard touchdown run against Rice on October 4, 1952, remains a memorable achievement in LSU football history.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

A Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1950, Richard “Richie” Nicolo was a dual-threat quarterback who could beat opponents with both his arm and his legs. He led the Sachems to consecutive Exchange Bowl championships in 1949 and 1950.

In the 1949 Exchange Bowl, his 50-yard touchdown pass to his brother Sardi as time expired tied Weymouth. Jimmy Kane’s extra point completed the dramatic 7–6 victory. The following year, Richie threw two touchdown passes and rushed for two more scores in a 30–12 win over Brockton, earning the game’s Most Valuable Player honors.

Nicolo continued his college football career at Boston College and Louisiana State University (LSU).
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1988

alumni.name: Christie Serino
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Set the career passing yards record at Saugus.
Went on to have a successful hockey coaching career. Coached in the Hockey East 1991 - 2005 (Assistant Coach at UNH 1991-1998; Head Coach at Merrimack 1999 - 2005).
Spent his final years as head coach, building Malden Catholic hockey program into a powerhouse (2005 - 2011). He led Malden Catholic to the Super 8 Championship in his final season in 2011.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Doug Mackie
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

2x Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All Scholastic (1974-1975). Named to Parade Magazine and Blue Chip Magazine High School All American Team in 1975. Went on to play college football at Ohio State for the legendary Woody Hayes. Injuries cost him some playing time during his college days. Went on to play professionally in the NFL for the New York Giants (1982), New Orleans Saints (1986), and Atlanta Falcons (1987) although he was mostly a practice player in the NFL. His greatest success as a professional was in the USFL where he played for the Tampa Bay Bandits (1983) and the New Jersey Generals (1984-1985). While playing for the New Jersey Generals he was selected as a 1984 College & Pro Football Newsweekly 2nd Team All-Pro along with running back Herschel Walker as he was part of the starting offensive line who helped Walker set the still standing, single-season, pro football rushing record of 2,411 yards.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Steve Gannon
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Went on to play college football at Holy Cross. He was a standout member of the defense for the Holy Cross football team during the late 1970s. Earned first team All-ECAC honors during his senior year, in addition to receiving the Davitt Award as the team’s top defensive lineman. As a senior led the team with 143 tackles, the most in recorded school history at the time. During his junior year in 1978, he helped lead the Crusaders to an overall record of 7-4, including victories over Air Force, Army and Boston College. A 2020 Inductee into the Holy Cross Athletic Hall of Fame. After college he had two NFL tryouts, one with the New York Giants and one with the Cincinnati Bengals both in 1980. After his playing days ended he got involved in coaching youth and high school football, being an assistant coach on John Nicolo's Sachems teams (2001-2004).

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1988

alumni.name: John Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic (1974, 1975) and 1975 Thom McCann North Shore Player of the Year and Boston Herald All-Scholastic, he captained Saugus to a share of the 1975 Northeastern Conference championship.
At Ithaca College, he starred in football and baseball: All-American running back on the 1979 Stagg Bowl (Division III National) champions; College World Series MVP on the 1980 Division III National Championship baseball team.
Three-time Ithaca College Athletic Hall of Fame inductee (1986 individual; 2014 football team; 2019 baseball team).
Later contributions: Rebuilt Saugus Pop Warner program; Saugus Sachems head football coach (2001–2004); interim Saugus High School Athletic Director (2003–2004).

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1987

alumni.name: Steve Peach
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1991.

A 3x Lynn Item All Scholastic (first player to ever make the team 3x). Greatest QB to ever come out of Saugus High. Was also an excellent baseball and basketball player. He was heavily recruited by Syracuse and Boston College, and he decided on going to Syracuse, where he started as a freshman. After that, he transferred to Boston College as a junior and was the backup to Doug Flutie and was also the punter.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1991

alumni.name: Darren McCullough
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1997.

Darren McCullough ranks among the best all-around players in Sachems history and is one of the few Saugus players to earn Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors twice.

As a junior in 1985, he recorded 123 tackles and four interceptions while playing linebacker and defensive back. On offense, he rushed for 442 yards and added 232 receiving yards, finishing with six total touchdowns.

As a senior in 1986, McCullough again led the team in tackles and rushed for 1,081 yards and 11 touchdowns. His standout performance came against Danvers, when he rushed for 225 yards and four touchdowns while also making 16 tackles. That effort earned him the Item/Coca-Cola Gold Helmet Award.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1997

alumni.name: Marc Fauci
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

A 2x Lynn Item All Scholastic. Boston Globe All Scholastic his senior season. Won the NEC Most Valuable Player Award in football during his senior year. A 2x co-captain as a junior and senior. Went on to play college football for Boston University. Led the Terriers football team during arguably its best season ever in 1993 when BU went 12-1 and finished the regular season with a perfect 11-0 mark, the first unbeaten and untied record in program history. A second-team All-America selection by The Sports Network and National Weekly Football Gazette and a third-team All-America selection by the Associated Press, Fauci played linebacker and ranks in the top five for career primary, assisted and total tackles. Was a 2010 Inductee into the Boston University Athletic Hall of Fame.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2000

alumni.name: Dan Schena
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2001.

A Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1990, Dan Schena was a tri-captain and the heart and soul of the Sachems’ 8–2 team, whose season remains a highlight in the program’s history.

Regarded as one of the finest linemen to wear a Sachems jersey, Schena recorded more than 100 tackles during his senior season. He continued his football career at Northeastern University.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2001

alumni.name: Mike Mabee
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

A Lynn Item All-Scholastic. A multi-sport star at Saugus High School. As co-captain and standout quarterback of the 1995 Sachems, Mabee helped end a school-record 34-game losing streak and led Saugus to a 6–5 finish—the program’s first winning season since 1990.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2006

alumni.name: LJ McKanas
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2007.

Captain his senior season. Played a big role in turning Saugus into a competitive program in the mid-90s. During his senior season he set records for most rushing yards and most touchdowns. He was selected Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All-Scholastic. He then went on to play college football at Northeastern University. After he redshirted his freshman season, he went on to become a four-year starter. During his redshirt freshman season he broke the NU rookie rushing record with 832 yards, averaging 92.4 yards per game. His Sophomore and Junior seasons were derailed due to injuries. During his senior season he set school records for most carries, 342, rushing yards, 1756, and rushing touchdowns, 14. For his senior season, he was named team MVP, All-New England, All-Conference and first-team Hanson All-America. He was also the winner of the Harry Agganis Award as the Outstanding Senior Football Player in New England. After college he appeared on the TV Show "Survivor" in 2014 where he finished in 9th place.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2007

alumni.name: Anthony “Beave” Barbanti
alumni.bio:
A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Anthony “Beave” Barbanti was a three-year starter on both the offensive and defensive lines and a cornerstone of the Sachems during his junior and senior seasons.

His senior season in 2003 was his finest: he recorded 75 tackles, including 11 tackles for loss, and three sacks. He was equally dominant on the offensive line, helping clear the way for Mike Nicolo’s record-setting rushing performances. Barbanti’s strength, consistency and two-way play made him a key part of Saugus’ success.
alumni.source: Profile supplied by Sal Nicolo; senior statistics corroborated by the 2003 Item All-Star clipping.

alumni.name: Mike Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 2026). A four-year starter and team captain his senior year, he set a then–single-game rushing record with 306 yards against Salem as a junior. He earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors that same season. Though injuries limited his senior year, his athletic success extended beyond football—he was an All-Scholastic selection in Winter Track as a sophomore and in Baseball as a junior.
He continued his football career at Curry College, where he was part of four consecutive New England Football Conference championship teams. He also contributed to Curry’s first-ever NCAA Division III playoff victory—fittingly, against his father John’s alma mater, Ithaca College.

alumni.name: Brett Reid
alumni.bio:
A three-year starting quarterback and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Brett Reid helped lead a resurgence in Sachems football. As a junior in 2007, he teamed with Tyler Trainor, Paul Sullivan and Mike Dean to guide Saugus to a 7–3 record—its first winning season since 1997 and its most wins since 1996.

Operating in a run-heavy offense, Reid rushed for 797 yards and 13 touchdowns that season. He and Dean helped Saugus repeat its 7–3 finish in 2008, with Reid contributing 800 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Justin Winn
alumni.bio:
Justin Winn earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors in both his junior and senior seasons. In 2013, he scored 19 rushing touchdowns (the statistics table lists 1,103 rushing yards; the supplied alumni text lists 1,108, a difference still under review), providing a standout individual performance during a difficult 3–8 season for the Sachems.

In 2014, Winn and running back Dan Cicciola helped lead Saugus to a 6–5 record. Winn rushed for 1,255 yards and set a school record with 22 rushing touchdowns.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Brandon Faiella
alumni.bio: A two-time captain and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Faiella was named the Lynn Item Defensive Player of the Year as a senior. He continued his football career as a linebacker for the Saint Anselm College Hawks. As of fall 2026, he is in his junior season.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Carlo Abate
alumni.bio:
A three-year starter at linebacker and a two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Carlo Abate was a cornerstone of the Sachems’ defense. As a junior in 1994, he recorded more than 120 tackles, including 22 against Lynn English in a performance that earned him Gold Helmet player of the game honors.

Despite shoulder and knee injuries, Abate led the Saugus defense as a senior in 1995 with 115 tackles, four interceptions and four fumble recoveries. He played a key role in ending the Sachems’ 34-game losing streak and helping the team achieve its first winning season in five years.
alumni.source: Profile contributed by Sal Nicolo.

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Shipulski
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Edward “Eddie” Shipulski was a major backfield star during one of Saugus High's finest football eras. A three-season player, he helped the Sachems win the 1939 North Shore championship and the 1941 Class C state championship. The 1940 yearbook singled him out as a sophomore standout after he scored twice in a 26–0 victory over Gloucester. By his senior season, Shipulski and Mike Harrington formed the backfield partnership the yearbook called its “touchdown twins.” Shipulski's 1941 highlights included touchdown runs of 70 yards against Gloucester, 57 yards against Amesbury, and 87 yards against Swampscott. A newspaper preview credited him with a team-leading 84 points entering Thanksgiving, despite an arm injury that limited his late-season action. He received Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention and also played varsity baseball.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1988

alumni.name: Michael “Mike” Garofano
alumni.bio: Michael Garofano helped lead Saugus High's return to organized football in 1914. A September newspaper feature identified him as captain and left halfback of a team being rebuilt after a lengthy interruption. By the time of a 1917 preseason report, Garofano was serving in France during World War I, and Saugus was preparing to select a replacement captain. His surviving clippings preserve both an early leader of the revived football program and a young Saugus serviceman whose life extended beyond the playing field.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Franklin “Oozo” Pike
alumni.bio: Franklin Pike was a powerful, versatile fullback at the center of Fred Beresford's unbeaten 1922 Saugus team. Contemporary coverage praised his strength as a runner and his ability to pass and kick, making him a threat in several parts of the game. He had already attracted notice in 1921, when a 75-yard interception return helped Saugus defeat Rockland. A later profile credited him with decisive performances against Rockland and Wellesley and described his development into one of the team's leading players. Pike represents the early generation that helped establish Saugus as a competitive football program.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Edward Amery
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1992.

Captain Edward Amery supplied leadership and versatility to Saugus High's unbeaten 1922 eleven. The contemporary profile of the team praised him as a passer, receiver, interceptor, and its leading punter. Alongside Franklin Pike, Lester Pool, and quarterback Forest Kenerson, Amery helped give a relatively light squad the skill and adaptability to compete successfully under Fred Beresford. His captaincy and contributions in several roles helped shape one of Saugus's earliest outstanding teams.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1992

alumni.name: John “Jack” Leahy
alumni.bio: John Leahy was a captain and fullback during Albion Rice's early years at Saugus. A newspaper feature compared his summer work delivering heavy blocks of ice with the conditioning associated with football celebrity Red Grange. The article identified Leahy as a junior and one of Rice's leading hopes for the following fall. The later yearbook account places him among the experienced players around whom the successful 1927 team was built, preserving his importance as both a backfield player and a veteran leader. He was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1992.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1992

alumni.name: Reginald “Reggie” Goss
alumni.bio: Reggie Goss was an experienced leader of Saugus football in the late 1920s. After contributing at end to the 1927 team that won seven of eleven games, he was elected captain for 1928. The yearbook records his work at quarterback and end, his responsibility for the team's punting, and his determination despite an injury carried over from the previous season. In the muddy Thanksgiving game against Mission High, he caught Stuart Kidder's long pass and continued downfield on a play that gained more than sixty yards. The account also recognizes Goss's academic achievement.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Foley
alumni.bio: Jim Foley earned a memorable place in the 1928 yearbook through his passing, tackling, and upbeat approach to football. Playing with one arm, he was praised for his judgment and effectiveness as well as his determination. The season account lists him among the quarterbacks and commends his backfield work against a heavier Mission High team on Thanksgiving. Foley's story offers a distinctive portrait of an early Saugus player whose teammates valued his ability, attitude, and willingness to take on the game's demands.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Stuart Kidder
alumni.bio: Stuart Kidder made a strong impression at fullback during the 1928 season. He won the fullback position and, according to the yearbook, gained more yardage than any other Saugus player that fall. His most vividly recalled play came against Mission High on Thanksgiving, when he escaped pressure and threw a long pass to Reggie Goss for a gain exceeding sixty yards. The yearbook regarded his combination of running ability and promise as one of the bright spots of a demanding season.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Muzzy
alumni.bio: James Muzzy was a versatile halfback and captain of Saugus High's 1930 football team. When the lettermen elected him, Coach Albion Rice described him as the squad's best all-around player. The yearbook tribute credited Muzzy with consistent running, blocking, tackling, and passing, and ranked him behind only Laurie Templeman as a scoring threat. His leadership helped define a team remembered in the yearbook as Saugus's best since the unbeaten 1922 eleven.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Laurence “Laurie” Templeman
alumni.bio: Laurence “Laurie” Templeman was one of Saugus High's outstanding running threats at the turn of the 1930s. In 1929, he scored both touchdowns in the 12–0 victory over Swampscott that the yearbook described as Saugus's first football win over that opponent. He also scored three long touchdowns in a victory over Rockport. The following season's tribute praised his speed, scoring, and ability to threaten opponents whenever he carried the ball. Together with captain Jim Muzzy, Templeman gave Coach Rice an accomplished backfield pairing.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Charles “Charlie” Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1999.

Charles Murphy was one of Saugus High's most widely recognized linemen of the early 1950s. A co-captain of the 1951 team, he earned places on the Boston Globe, Boston Post, and Lynn Item All-Scholastic selections. The Globe's main team identified him at guard, while the Item listed him as a senior guard. R.A.A. award material provides further recognition of his line play. These surviving selections document Murphy's distinction during the years immediately following the Exchange Bowl teams.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1999

alumni.name: Jim Driscoll
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Jim Driscoll was a Lynn Item All-Scholastic halfback on Saugus High's 1950 Exchange Bowl championship team. His versatility helped the Sachems early in the season, when he moved to quarterback while Richie Nicolo was unavailable. The Football Folio records his passing connection with Charlie Woodell and his later contributions as a runner. Driscoll helped give the 8–2 Sachems an adaptable backfield during the season that ended with a 30–12 Exchange Bowl victory over Brockton.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2006

alumni.name: Tony Serino
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2004.

Tony Serino contributed to the backfield during Saugus's successful transition from the Exchange Bowl years into the early 1950s. The 1950 Football Folio records two touchdown runs against Chelsea during the season that produced a second consecutive Exchange Bowl championship. In 1951, he shared the captaincy with Charlie Murphy and earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition as a utility back. His scoring, leadership, and regional selection marked his contributions during these seasons.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2004

alumni.name: Robert “Bob” Belyea
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1999.

Bob Belyea was an honored lineman on Saugus High's 1953 North Shore League championship team. The 1954 yearbook records four years of football participation and identifies Belyea and Bill Whittredge as first-string selections on the Lynn All-Star team. The Boston Globe also named Belyea among its All-Scholastic reserves at guard in December 1953. His individual recognition complemented his contributions to a championship team.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1954 Tontoquonian, senior biography and senior-year class history
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1999

alumni.name: Bill Whittredge
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1996.

Bill Whittredge helped give Saugus its productive backfield during the 1953 North Shore League championship season. The 1954 yearbook records that he had been voted the best back of the previous year and names him, alongside Bob Belyea, as a first-string selection on the Lynn All-Star team during the class's championship senior year. The yearbook preserves his contributions to John Janusas's title-winning team.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1954 Tontoquonian, junior- and senior-year class histories
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1996

alumni.name: John Leahy
alumni.bio: John Leahy helped lead Saugus High to the 1953 North Shore League championship as a co-captain with Doug MacNeill. His senior biography records four years of football, and the class history identifies both captains as second-string selections on the Lynn All-Star team. The Sachems finished 6–1–1 in regular-season play and secured the title with a 33–6 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody. Leahy's captaincy and individual recognition preserve his place among the leaders of that championship team.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1954 Tontoquonian, senior biography and class history

alumni.name: Douglas “Doug” MacNeill
alumni.bio: Doug MacNeill was a co-captain of Saugus High's 1953 North Shore League champions and a four-year football participant. The yearbook identifies him and fellow captain John Leahy as second-string Lynn All-Star selections. MacNeill also participated in basketball and baseball, reflecting the broad athletic involvement common to that generation of Sachems. His leadership helped define a season capped by a decisive Thanksgiving win over Peabody and remembered as a championship autumn for the school.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1954 Tontoquonian, Douglas MacNeill biography and senior-year history

alumni.name: Bob Piwowarski
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2004.

Bob Piwowarski was a prominent runner on Saugus High's 6–3 team in 1954 and earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition at back. The yearbook recalls his touchdown during the opening 20–0 win over Revere and his contribution to an offense that also featured Mal Rice, Fred Case, and Charlie Lawrence. His newspaper selection and repeated appearances in the season accounts place him among the notable Sachems of the middle 1950s.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2004

alumni.name: Richard “Dick” Rohrbacher
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2002.

Dick Rohrbacher was a captain and a recognized lineman for Saugus High in the late 1950s. The Item selected him at tackle on its 1957 North Shore All-Star team, listing him as a senior. His selection provides a contemporary record of a Sachem earning regional distinction in the late 1950s.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2002

alumni.name: John Naples
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2002.

John Naples was a captain and first-team regional honoree for Saugus High in 1958. The Item's North Shore All-Star roster selected him at guard and identified him as a senior. His captaincy and selection recognized the line play behind Saugus football in the late 1950s.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1959 senior biography for John James Naples
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2002

alumni.name: William Banks
alumni.bio: William Banks earned Boston Globe recognition for his line play at Saugus High in 1958. The newspaper's December 7 All-Scholastic feature named him among its reserves at guard. His inclusion documents the Sachems' contribution to the region's accomplished linemen.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1959 senior biography for William Clifford Banks

alumni.name: Ron “Ronnie” Barressi
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

Ron Barressi was a captain and regional All-Star during Saugus High's rebuilding years in the middle 1960s. The Item's 1964 North Shore team recognized him as its utility back, listing him as a senior. His selection is a reminder that individual Sachems earned distinction even outside the program's championship seasons.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2000

alumni.name: John Dancewicz
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

John Dancewicz was a co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 football team in 1966 and a first-team Lynn Item All-Star. His versatility is preserved in two contemporary records: the yearbook identifies him as a back, while the Item honored him at tackle. Dancewicz also served as senior class president and appears among the year's National Merit finalists, giving his profile a documented combination of football leadership and academic accomplishment.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1967 Tontoquonian, senior officers, honors and commencement
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2000

alumni.name: James “Jim” Mancuso
alumni.bio: Jim Mancuso was a first-team Lynn Item All-Star tackle on Saugus High's successful 1966 team. The newspaper listed him at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, and the yearbook preserves his individual football portrait. His senior biography records four years of football and hockey and identifies him as a hockey co-captain. Mancuso combined individual football recognition with participation across several sports.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1967 Tontoquonian, James Joseph Mancuso senior entry

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Maguire
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Edward Maguire was a backfield leader and co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 team in 1966. He earned first-team Lynn Item All-Star recognition at back, joining teammates John Dancewicz and Jim Mancuso on the selected team. The yearbook preserves his co-captain portrait alongside Dancewicz and Paul Uga, documenting the leadership group behind one of Saugus's strongest seasons of the decade.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1967 yearbook, Edward James Maguire senior entry
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1988

alumni.name: James “Jim” Fauci
alumni.bio: James Fauci captained Saugus High during Buzz Harvey's first season as head coach in 1937. His senior yearbook praised his alert, determined play and the example he set for his teammates. The team opened with five consecutive victories, making Fauci a useful representative of the players who helped establish Harvey's successful Saugus tenure. His yearbook tribute preserves an important leadership figure from the late 1930s.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Earl Hanson
alumni.bio: Earl Hanson was a three-season football participant and captain of Saugus High's 1938 team. His senior yearbook remembered a quiet leader whose courage helped set the tone for his teammates. The Sachems finished 6–4 and closed with a 6–0 Thanksgiving victory over Danvers. Hanson's captaincy links the early years of Buzz Harvey's program with the greater success that followed in 1939.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1939 senior biography and fall 1938 football section

alumni.name: Michael “Mike” Light
alumni.bio: Michael Light was a co-captain of Saugus High's 1958 football team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition at end. His senior biography records three seasons of football and four years of hockey, preserving the range of his athletic participation. Light shared the football captaincy with John Naples.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1959 senior entry for Michael Charles Light

alumni.name: David Russell “Dave” Mathews
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1989.

David Russell Mathews was a football and hockey co-captain at Saugus High and a four-year participant in football, hockey and baseball. The Item selected him at back on its 1959 North Shore All-Star team. His senior yearbook remembered his broad athletic ability, and the football portrait collection preserves him among the leaders of Saugus's recognized 1959 championship team. He was part of the final graduating cohort to play under John Janusas at Saugus.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 1989

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Burt
alumni.bio: Richard Burt was a fullback on Saugus High's recognized 1959 championship team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition. His senior biography records four years each of football and baseball and specifically praises his running for the champion football team. The yearbook's award list also names him as recipient of the John A. W. Pearce Football Award. Burt combined team success with regional recognition and a school football award.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1960 yearbook: Richard Cochrane Burt biography, printed p. 22, and award list

alumni.name: Louis “Lou” O’Neil
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Louis O'Neil was a four-year football participant and captain whose line play earned first-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition in 1968. His senior biography also lists hockey, track and weightlifting, reflecting his broad athletic involvement. The 1969 yearbook's football roster identifies him as a captain during a season in which Saugus recovered from a difficult start to finish with three consecutive victories. His first-team selection recognized his line play at the end of the decade.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1969 yearbook senior entry, printed p. 126, and football section
SHS Hall of Fame · induction class 2006

alumni.name: James “Jim” Canole
alumni.bio: James Canole was a captain and three-season football participant at Saugus High. The Item named him to its 1968 North Shore All-Star second team as a utility player. His senior biography also records track, volleyball and gymnastics participation, while the football section preserves his captaincy and role in the team's late-season improvement. His regional recognition and leadership marked his contribution to the Class of 1969.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

sources.label: 1969 senior entry for James William Canole and football roster
